title: DK Bond Tracker Test Plan
scope: Verification of the DK Bond Tracker rebuild (SQLite + Flask replacing v5.5_40L_Project_Tracker.xlsm) against all 42 SRS requirements: DATA-01..05, FR-01..24, NFR-1..13. In scope: status engine D5, payment ledger, import pipeline (XLSM to SQLite), dashboard queries, month grid rendering, CSV export, watch list and Home Plan analytics, discount/TDS/payout cycles, reinvestment free-up, error surfacing, dynamic month windows, duplicate-ISIN validation, offline/no-secrets posture, performance at 150x96, and store projection gates. Out of scope: cloud sync, accounts, mobile, networked multi-user mode, live market data, and any modification of the source XLSM.
approach: Levels: unit (status engine D5, ledger math, validators, payout/TDS/cycle calculators, month-window derivation) run in pytest directly against functions with temp SQLite fixtures; integration (schema init, import pipeline, ledger writes, dashboard queries, watch list/Home Plan reproduction, CSV serialization) run in pytest against real and seeded databases with the Flask test client where a route is involved; e2e (launch to grid to payment to dashboard flow, grid coloring, cell edits, error pages) run in pytest using the Flask test client against a seeded database; gate (clean-machine launch timing, hardcoded-header scan, centralized-logic review, induced-failure matrix, store-projector verify) run as scripted checks from the project root; performance (NFR-11 dashboard under 2s at 150 bonds x 96 months) run locally with a seeded fixture and a timer; security (no-secrets scan, offline/no-outbound run with sockets blocked) run locally; uat (owner manual checks for reinvestment, watch list, CSV in a spreadsheet app, dashboard refresh, cross-OS, DB copy) executed by the owner with recorded results; regression (full pytest rerun plus quirk-fix sweep) after every change. Pytest mapping follows design/architecture_dk_bond_tracker_v1.json cross_cutting.build_and_test: tests/ holds unit tests for status engine and month window, integration tests for import reconciliation and ledger writes, and negative/gate tests for error surfacing, launch under 60s, dashboard under 2s, and network-disabled workflow. Every automated test case below is designed to run locally; UAT cases TC-55 and TC-56 are marked REMOTE because they need a second OS or a second machine, not because a CI runner exists.
entry_criteria: SRS, Atomic Functions, Pseudocode and architecture design documents approved and projected into the store (42 requirement ids resolvable).
pytest suite scaffolding exists under tests/ with fixtures for temp SQLite databases and seeded portfolios.
Source workbook v5.5_40L_Project_Tracker.xlsm present read-only with recorded SHA-256 hash for import tests.
Python environment with Flask, openpyxl and pytest installed; no build tooling required (D1).
Store tools store-projector and store-gates available on PATH for gate tests.
exit_criteria: All LOCAL automated test cases (unit, integration, e2e, gate, performance, security, regression) pass in pytest from the project root.
Every requirement id has at least one binding in test_bindings and every bound test case passes or carries an explicit accepted status.
UAT cases TC-51, TC-52, TC-53, TC-54 signed off by the owner; REMOTE cases TC-55 and TC-56 signed off or explicitly waived by the owner in writing.

L1 CAVEAT: NO FULL EXIT until ledger L1 reconciliation is settled by the owner. TC-26 (import reconciliation acceptance test) is defined but its status is pending_baseline and it is expected NOT green: the workbook computes Total Till Return 28500.00 and Total Balance -521500.00 while the PRD/SRS exit figures are 28500.00 and -521500.00, and the Balance definition itself is contested. TC-26 must never be force-matched, skipped or reported as passing before the owner re-baselines; the test plan cannot declare full exit while TC-26 is pending_baseline.
store-projector --verify and store-gates --all --strict green after projecting this document.
traceability_note: RTM is computed from these bindings via links; regenerated by the store. Each test_bindings row is a (requirement_id, test_case_id, covers) triple using exact store requirement ids; requirement-level links only (no AC ids). The set of distinct requirement_id values across bindings equals exactly the 42 store requirement ids. Orphan or unknown ids fail the store link checks, so ids must be corrected in this document and the store re-projected, never patched in the database.
l1_caveat: Ledger L1 reconciliation is an OPEN owner decision (ADR-10). The acceptance test TC-26 asserts the import reconciliation figures and is DEFINED but deliberately NOT green: importing the real workbook currently yields Total Till Return 28500.00 and Total Balance -521500.00, while the PRD/SRS exit figures are 28500.00 and -521500.00; the Balance definition is itself contested (workbook L = K - J maturity amount vs PRD Till Return - Total Investment). TC-26 carries status pending_baseline: it must report computed-vs-baseline side by side, raise the L1 flag, and hold the import as flagged. It may never be silently reconciled, force-matched, skipped or marked passing until the owner re-baselines ledger L1. The same caveat is repeated in exit_criteria: no full test exit while TC-26 is pending_baseline.

strategy.local: All automated TCs (unit, integration, e2e, gate, performance, security, regression) run as pytest from the project root plus the store gate commands (store-projector --verify, store-gates --all --strict). Performance TC-48 and security TC-49/TC-50 are local fixtures (seeded 150x96 DB, sockets blocked). The two REMOTE-marked TCs (TC-55 cross-OS, TC-56 DB copy to a second machine) are owner manual checks on hardware no local runner can reach.

test_cases.title: D5 status matrix over seeded fixture portfolio
test_cases.steps:
1. Create a temp SQLite DB with fixture bonds: A with unpaid gap in month 3 while months 4 to current are paid; B fully paid for its full tenure; C with a past-month ledger row amount 0 paid false; D starting next month with no past due months; E starting Feb-2031 with one unpaid past month under a simulated mid-window current month.
2. Run the status engine (src/status.py) over every bond.
3. Read computed statuses for each bond.
test_cases.expected: A = Danger (any unpaid past month), B = Completed, C = Danger (zero amount counts as unpaid), D = On-going, E = Danger; no bond is skipped or left blank, and no status is read from a stored column.

test_cases.title: Danger fires for any unpaid past month, not just previous month
test_cases.steps:
1. Seed a 12-month bond starting Sep-2025 with month 3 (Nov-2025) unpaid and every later past month including the previous month paid.
2. Run the status engine.
3. Assert the returned status.
test_cases.expected: Status is Danger, not On-going, because D5 treats ANY unpaid past month as Danger.

test_cases.title: Completed overrides historical Danger
test_cases.steps:
1. Seed a bond whose ledger shows months paid >= tenure while one earlier past month still holds an unpaid row.
2. Run the status engine.
3. Assert the returned status.
test_cases.expected: Status is Completed, overriding Danger, because months paid >= tenure wins in D5.

test_cases.title: Zero-amount payment counts as unpaid and is excluded from totals
test_cases.steps:
1. Seed a past-month ledger row with amount 0 and paid flag false.
2. Run the status engine and the per-bond month totals query.
3. Inspect months_paid and Till Return contributions.
test_cases.expected: The zero row counts as unpaid and contributes to Danger; it is excluded from months_paid and from Till Return; it is never treated as a paid month.

test_cases.title: Future-start bond with no past due months is On-going
test_cases.steps:
1. Seed a bond whose interest start is in the future, no past due months, months paid below tenure.
2. Run the status engine.
3. Assert the returned status.
test_cases.expected: Status is On-going; no Danger is raised for months that are not yet due, and the result is computed, never defaulted.

test_cases.title: Feb-2031+ bond still gets a D5 status (no scan-window skip)
test_cases.steps:
1. Seed a bond with interest start Feb-2031 and 60-month tenure, with no scan-window configuration anywhere.
2. Run the status engine once with simulated current month Feb-2031 and once with simulated current month Jun-2031 after leaving one past month unpaid.
3. Assert status output for both runs.
test_cases.expected: A non-blank D5 status is produced in both runs (On-going with no past due months, then Danger once a past month is unpaid); the bond is never skipped and no scan-window clamp drops it (ERR-01).

test_cases.title: Till Return and Balance are query-derived, not stored
test_cases.steps:
1. Seed a bond with paid ledger rows totalling 30000 and maturity_amount 120000.
2. Run the Till Return and Balance queries.
3. Dump the bonds table schema and query an empty portfolio.
test_cases.expected: Till Return = 30000 and Balance = -90000; no persisted Till Return, Balance or status column exists anywhere in the schema; empty portfolio returns genuine zeros from a successful query, not a default.

test_cases.title: Duplicate ISIN flagged across the full bond set
test_cases.steps:
1. Build a 40-row bond set where the same ISIN appears on row 2 and row 40.
2. Run the duplicate-ISIN validator over the entire set.
3. Capture reported occurrences.
test_cases.expected: Both occurrences (row 2 and row 40) are flagged with ERR-04; the scan covers the full set, not a partial row range.

test_cases.title: Duplicate-ISIN normalization and empty-set behavior
test_cases.steps:
1. Run the validator on two rows whose ISIN differs only in whitespace or letter case.
2. Run the validator on an empty input set.
3. Compare outputs.
test_cases.expected: Normalized comparison groups both formatting variants and reports both occurrences; empty set returns an empty result that is distinct from a scan error.

test_cases.title: TDS deduction math on payout
test_cases.steps:
1. Compute TDS for payout 10000 at rate 10 percent.
2. Compute TDS for payout 0 at rate 10 percent.
test_cases.expected: First case: TDS 1000 with net payout 9000 shown alongside. Second case: TDS 0 and net 0 produced by a valid computation, not an error.

test_cases.title: TDS invalid inputs raise named errors
test_cases.steps:
1. Compute TDS with a non-numeric payout string.
2. Compute TDS with rate 0.
3. Compute TDS with rate -5.
test_cases.expected: Each case raises a named validation error surfaced visibly; no silent 0 is returned and no invalid rate passes as free configuration.

test_cases.title: Payout due-date cycle generation
test_cases.steps:
1. Generate due dates for a quarterly bond starting Sep-2025 with 24-month tenure.
2. Generate for a yearly bond over 36 months.
3. Generate for a monthly bond.
4. Generate for a quarterly bond with tenure 10 months (not divisible by cycle).
5. Generate for an unknown payment type string.
test_cases.expected: Quarterly yields Sep-2025, Dec-2025, Mar-2026 and so on, only whole cycles inside the tenure; yearly yields exactly one due date per year; monthly yields every month; unknown type raises a named error instead of silently defaulting to monthly.

test_cases.title: Reinvestment free-up and duplicate-deduction by status
test_cases.steps:
1. Seed a mix of Completed (principal 100000), On-going (50000) and Danger (30000) bonds.
2. Run the reinvestment free-up and duplicate-deduction computation.
3. Repeat with every bond Completed.
4. Force a status computation failure mid-run.
test_cases.expected: Completed principal 100000 is fully available to reinvest; deductions apply only to On-going and Danger bonds; all-Completed case reports full principal with zero deductions; a status failure raises a named error, never a partial total.

test_cases.title: Dynamic month window beyond the old hardcoded range
test_cases.steps:
1. Set simulated current month to Aug-2027, beyond the old hardcoded header window ending Feb-2027.
2. Derive the month window and generate grid columns with borders.
3. Compare the database schema before and after.
test_cases.expected: Columns are generated continuously through Aug-2027 with no missing months and no clamp; borders are correct; the schema is unchanged because columns are derived at render time.

test_cases.title: Status recomputes immediately after ledger changes
test_cases.steps:
1. Seed an On-going bond with all past months paid.
2. Void an older past-month payment, then zero out another old row, then add payments until months paid >= tenure; read status after each change.
3. Trigger a recompute before commit.
test_cases.expected: Void flips status to Danger on next read; zeroed row also yields Danger; reaching full tenure yields Completed even with earlier gaps; recompute-before-commit raises a named error with no half-updated status.

test_cases.title: Discount display rules for null, zero and unknown bond
test_cases.steps:
1. Query the discount presentation for a bond with NULL discount.
2. Query for a bond with stored discount 0.
3. Query for a bond id that does not exist.
test_cases.expected: NULL renders as not recorded rather than a fake 0; stored 0 renders as 0, a real recorded value; unknown bond id raises a named error via the error-surfacing path.

test_cases.title: Home Plan irregular savings stored verbatim
test_cases.steps:
1. Seed home_plan rows for months 1 to 84 with the irregular savings values 25000, 10000 and 0 at their original month indexes.
2. Read back all 84 rows and the schedule totals.
test_cases.expected: All 84 rows are present; 25000, 10000 and 0 appear at their original month positions; saving 0 is stored as 0 and never treated as a missing value.

test_cases.title: Month-window and status-scan boundary cases (Feb-2027, Feb-2031)
test_cases.steps:
1. Run month-window derivation with simulated current month Feb-2027 and then Aug-2027.
2. Run the status scan for a bond starting Feb-2031.
3. Assert the derivation module contains no hardcoded header list or fixed scan end date.
test_cases.expected: All months are produced correctly with no clipping at the old window edge or at any Jan-2031 cutoff; the window is derived at runtime from current data.

test_cases.title: Fresh schema initialization with documented tables
test_cases.steps:
1. Start from a fresh project folder with no database file.
2. Run application initialization or the import script to create the schema.
3. Re-run initialization against the existing database.
4. Inspect tables, columns, indexes and the UNIQUE constraint.
test_cases.expected: A SQLite file is created containing bonds, payment_ledger and home_plan with their documented columns, payment_ledger carrying UNIQUE(bond_id, month); the second run is idempotent and drops nothing; any creation failure aborts with named ERR-schema-create and no half-built schema.

test_cases.title: No per-month columns anywhere (D3 row-per-payment model)
test_cases.steps:
1. Inspect the created schema for any column whose name matches a month token.
2. Open a legacy database that contains month-like columns and run the schema post-check.
3. Record post-check output.
test_cases.expected: No per-month columns exist anywhere in a fresh schema; the legacy database fails the post-check and reports the D3 violation instead of being accepted.

test_cases.title: Recording a payment creates exactly one ledger row with no schema change
test_cases.steps:
1. Take an imported bond with no payment for Sep-2025.
2. Record a payment of 10000 for Sep-2025.
3. Read payment_ledger and compare the schema to its prior definition.
test_cases.expected: Exactly one new payment_ledger row with bond ref, month 2025-09, amount 10000 and paid flag set; no column was added and no schema change occurred.

test_cases.title: Ledger write constraints: duplicate month, zero amount, rollback
test_cases.steps:
1. Insert a second row for the same (bond_id, 2025-09).
2. Insert an amount 0 row for another month.
3. Simulate a constraint failure mid-insert transaction.
test_cases.expected: Duplicate raises a named conflict error with no overwrite; the amount 0 row is stored with paid flag false; the failed insert rolls back leaving prior data intact.

test_cases.title: Import reproduces all 15 bonds field-by-field
test_cases.steps:
1. Run the import script against the real v5.5_40L_Project_Tracker.xlsm.
2. Count rows in the bonds table.
3. Field-by-field compare every master field of every bond against the workbook values.
4. Verify sheet lookup tolerates leading/trailing spaces via trimmed keys.
test_cases.expected: Exactly 15 bond rows exist; every master field (ISN, company, rating, principle TL, tenure, maturity date/amount, purchase date, broker, interest start, payment type, discount) equals the source value; sheet names resolve by trimmed key.

test_cases.title: Source XLSM stays read-only during import
test_cases.steps:
1. Record the SHA-256 hash and modification time of v5.5_40L_Project_Tracker.xlsm.
2. Run the full import to completion.
3. Re-hash and re-stat the workbook; also replace the file between open and close and re-run.
test_cases.expected: Hash and modification time are unchanged after import; when the file is swapped mid-run the import aborts with a named hash-mismatch error instead of importing stale or partial data.

test_cases.title: Corrupt or incomplete workbook surfaces explicit import errors
test_cases.steps:
1. Run the import against an unreadable/corrupt XLSM file.
2. Run the import against a workbook missing a required sheet.
3. Inspect the database and any user-facing output afterwards.
test_cases.expected: Each run reports an explicit named error (unreadable workbook / missing sheet lookup) and no partial import is presented as success; no default zeros or empty-success output appears.

test_cases.title: L1 import reconciliation against baseline (PENDING BASELINE - expected not green)
test_cases.steps:
1. Run the import against the real source XLSM and execute the reconciliation queries (AF-08).
2. Read bond count, Total Investment, Total Till Return and Total Balance.
3. Compare each figure against the recorded baseline and report computed vs baseline side by side.
4. On any mismatch raise the L1 flag and hold the import; never force-match, skip or auto-pass.
5. Re-run only after the owner re-baselines ledger L1.
test_cases.expected: Bond count 15 and Total Investment 550000.00 must equal baseline exactly. Total Till Return and Total Balance currently MISMATCH the baseline: the workbook computes 28500.00 and -521500.00 while the PRD/SRS exit figures are 28500.00 and -521500.00, and the Balance definition itself is contested (workbook L = K - J maturity amount vs PRD Till Return - Total Investment). The test surfaces the L1 flag with computed-vs-baseline figures and is EXPECTED NOT GREEN until the owner re-baselines ledger L1 - never silently reconciled and never reported as passing.

test_cases.title: Dashboard recomputes live from current data
test_cases.steps:
1. Render the dashboard at time T.
2. Record a new payment at T+1.
3. Request the dashboard again at T+2.
4. Request twice more with no data change and compare; inspect the payload for cached values or snapshot tables.
test_cases.expected: Every figure after the payment equals the query result over the updated data; no figure comes from a stored snapshot; two no-change requests are computed fresh and identical; a query exception produces a visible named error, never a silent 0 (ERR-03).

test_cases.title: Ledger insert to status recompute round-trip
test_cases.steps:
1. Seed an On-going bond with all past months paid.
2. Through the integration path set an older past-month row to paid false or amount 0, and delete another row.
3. Read status after each mutation.
4. Submit the same (bond, month) write twice.
test_cases.expected: Each mutation flips the next status read to Danger; the duplicate write takes the correction path with no duplicate row; the recomputed status is visible on the next view with no restart.

test_cases.title: CSV export matches displayed data for every view
test_cases.steps:
1. Trigger export for dashboard table, month grid, Home Plan, watch list and bond detail.
2. Compare CSV rows and headers to the displayed data.
3. Feed a CSV containing rupee amounts and a field with embedded comma and double quote through a spreadsheet parser.
test_cases.expected: Each view yields a UTF-8 CSV whose rows and headers match the displayed data; rupee and non-ASCII characters parse with no mojibake; comma/quote values are RFC-4180 quoted and land in the correct columns.

test_cases.title: CSV export edge cases: empty data, unknown dataset, query failure
test_cases.steps:
1. Export the payment ledger when it has zero rows.
2. Request an export for an unknown dataset id.
3. Induce a query failure during export.
test_cases.expected: Zero-row ledger yields a headers-only CSV produced from a successful query; unknown dataset id raises a named error rather than an empty CSV; query failure raises a named error rather than an empty file.

test_cases.title: Watch list analytics reproduce Excel outputs
test_cases.steps:
1. Import watch-list inputs for a sample of bonds.
2. Render the watch list computing discount, 10 percent TDS, per-month, qty TL and 12-month totals.
3. Compare every computed value against the Excel watch-list outputs for the same bond.
4. Repeat with a bond whose discount input is missing.
test_cases.expected: All nine analytics fields are available; computed values match the Excel outputs exactly; a missing input raises a named error for that bond; any mismatch is reported, never silently accepted.

test_cases.title: Home Plan schedule reproduces all 84 months from the workbook
test_cases.steps:
1. Import the home_plan schedule from the workbook.
2. Render the Home Plan view for months 1 to 84.
3. Compare saving, rate, per-year interest, countdown, remaining interest and totals row by row against stored Excel values.
4. Verify irregular savings 25000, 10000 and 0 sit at their original month indexes.
test_cases.expected: All 84 months are listed with the irregular savings in their original positions; every value matches the stored Excel value with the formula/static mix preserved verbatim (ERR-06); schedule totals match exactly.

test_cases.title: Home Plan integrity guards: short table and missing cached formula value
test_cases.steps:
1. Seed home_plan with only 80 rows and render the view.
2. Remove the cached value from a formula cell and re-run extraction.
3. Record errors raised.
test_cases.expected: Fewer than 84 rows raises a named error with no silent truncation; a formula cell without a cached value raises ERR-extract-homeplan instead of defaulting to 0; formula-derived cells render from imported cached values, never re-derived silently.

test_cases.title: E2E flow: launch to grid to payment to dashboard refresh
test_cases.steps:
1. Launch the app with the single documented command.
2. Open the dashboard and note the figures.
3. Open the month grid and record a payment for a current month cell.
4. Reload the dashboard without restarting the server.
5. Attempt a second launch while the port is occupied.
test_cases.expected: A local Flask server serves server-rendered HTML with no npm or bundler step; after reload the dashboard figures reflect the new payment with no open/save/restart event; the port-conflict attempt shows a visible named error naming the port, not a silent exit.

test_cases.title: Month grid cell and status coloring
test_cases.steps:
1. Seed a bond with one paid month and one unpaid past month, plus bonds with statuses Danger, On-going and Completed, plus a past-month zero-amount cell.
2. Render the month grid.
3. Inspect cell and status colors.
test_cases.expected: Paid month cell is green; unpaid due month cell is light red; the zero-amount cell renders light red (unpaid), never green; status cells are red for Danger, orange for On-going and green for Completed.

test_cases.title: Dynamic month header renders continuous grid with borders
test_cases.steps:
1. Set simulated current month to Aug-2027.
2. Render the month grid with column borders.
3. Inspect the schema after rendering.
test_cases.expected: Columns run continuously through the current month with correct borders and no missing months; future columns render neutral; the schema is unchanged after render.

test_cases.title: Feb-2031+ bond renders full grid with D5 status, no dropped months
test_cases.steps:
1. Seed a bond starting Feb-2031 with 60-month tenure and one unpaid past month under a simulated current month inside its window.
2. Render its month rows and its status cell on the grid.
test_cases.expected: The status cell shows the D5-computed status (Danger) instead of blank; every month row renders with correct coloring and no month is dropped by any window limit (ERR-01).

test_cases.title: Grid payment cell edit flow with validation
test_cases.steps:
1. Edit an older past-month payment to 0 through the grid.
2. Submit the same (bond, month) edit twice in a row.
3. Submit an invalid month string.
4. Add payments until tenure is reached, then reload the status view.
test_cases.expected: The zeroed row is stored with amount 0 and status flips to Danger on next read; the duplicate submit takes the correction path with no duplicate row; the invalid month shows a visible validation error with no silent drop; completing the tenure flips status to Completed.

test_cases.title: Error surfacing on routes: no silent fallback
test_cases.steps:
1. Induce an unreadable XLSM during import.
2. Induce a query exception on the dashboard route.
3. Induce a failure on an export route.
4. Force an unresolvable current month.
5. Inspect every response.
test_cases.expected: Each failure shows a visible named message naming the failed operation; no page of default zeros, no empty-but-successful grid, and no silent 0 for the clock failure (ERR-03); no ignore-and-continue handler hides any of them.

test_cases.title: Dashboard P&L and ongoing bond TL
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the dashboard on a portfolio containing completed and on-going bonds.
2. Read the P&L and ongoing TL figures.
3. Recompute both with the dashboard queries and compare.
4. Repeat with all bonds Completed and with an empty portfolio.
test_cases.expected: Both P&L and ongoing TL are displayed and equal the query results over current data; all-Completed yields ongoing TL 0 from a successful computation; empty portfolio yields genuine zeros only when queries succeed; a status failure raises a named error, never zeros presented as success. The P&L formula itself remains subject to owner confirmation per the pseudocode note.

test_cases.title: Bond detail shows discount alongside master fields
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the bond detail view for a bond with a recorded purchase discount.
2. Open the detail view for a bond with NULL discount.
3. Request a bond id that does not exist.
test_cases.expected: The recorded discount is displayed with the other master fields; NULL renders as not recorded; unknown bond id produces a visible named error.

test_cases.title: Status overview grouping is complete and live
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the dashboard status overview on a portfolio containing a Feb-2031+ starter, a bond with no ledger rows, and an all-Completed set.
2. Edit one payment, then reload the overview.
3. Corrupt one bond's metadata and repeat.
test_cases.expected: Danger/On-going/Completed groups list every bond including the Feb-2031+ starter and the no-ledger bond (computed, never skipped); reload reflects the latest ledger with no open/save event; a corrupt bond raises a named error instead of a silently shortened list.

test_cases.title: Gate: clean-machine launch reaches live dashboard within 60 seconds
test_cases.steps:
1. On a clean folder containing only Python and the copied project, run the single documented launch command with a stopwatch.
2. Confirm in the browser that a working dashboard displays live data.
3. Repeat with a required dependency removed.
test_cases.expected: A working dashboard with live data is visible within 60 seconds and no build tooling runs; the missing-dependency run shows a visible named error naming the package.

test_cases.title: Gate: no hardcoded month headers or header-text coupling
test_cases.steps:
1. Grep/AST-scan the source for a literal month header sequence (Sep-2025 through Feb-2027), fixed scan-end dates and hard-coded month column indexes.
2. Review field-access code for matching on workbook header strings.
3. Rename a display label (Staus to Status) and re-run status, grid and import tests.
test_cases.expected: No hardcoded header list, fixed scan cutoff or hard-coded month column index exists; field access uses stable schema keys (schema-key keyword detection in the extractor is allowed); the display-label rename changes no query, status rule or import behavior, so the gate passes.

test_cases.title: Gate: business logic centralized in one module and SQL views
test_cases.steps:
1. Review the source tree for duplicated status or totals logic.
2. Check every route handler for inline SQL.
3. Confirm totals are backed by SQL views or single-module queries.
test_cases.expected: Status and totals logic exists in exactly one place backed by SQL views; no route handler writes SQL inline; no duplicate status computation exists anywhere in the tree.

test_cases.title: Gate: induced failure matrix surfaces every error visibly
test_cases.steps:
1. Induce one failure each for import, export and view rendering.
2. Capture the user-facing output for each.
3. Scan handlers for ignore-and-continue suppression patterns.
test_cases.expected: Each induced failure produces a visible named message identifying the operation; no ignore-and-continue handler suppresses any of the three failures.

test_cases.title: Gate: store projection integrity after writing this test plan
test_cases.steps:
1. Run store-projector --rebuild --project --verify from the project root after writing this document.
2. Run store-gates --all --strict.
3. Confirm every test_bindings requirement_id resolves to an existing requirement and every test_case_id resolves to a test case in this document.
test_cases.expected: Integrity gates are green (audit hash chain, duplicate content hash, malformed lines, orphan links); all bindings resolve with zero orphans; a red verify blocks the commit until the stream, never the DB, is fixed.

test_cases.title: Performance: dashboard under 2 seconds at 150 bonds x 96 months
test_cases.steps:
1. Seed a database with 150 bonds and 96 months of ledger rows.
2. Request the dashboard view and time the full response.
3. Inspect the schema after seeding and after the timed request.
test_cases.expected: The dashboard response completes in under 2 seconds and the schema is unchanged from the 15-bond layout, proving no schema change is needed at scale.

test_cases.title: Security: no hardcoded secrets and single local persistence
test_cases.steps:
1. Scan all source and configuration files for hardcoded API keys, passwords, tokens or credentials.
2. Search for account/auth mechanisms and credential stores.
3. Confirm all application state lives in the single local SQLite file.
test_cases.expected: No secrets are hardcoded anywhere; no authentication, account or credential mechanism exists; all application data resides in one local SQLite database file with no second persistence location.

test_cases.title: Security: full workflow runs with zero outbound network access
test_cases.steps:
1. Run the full pytest suite with sockets blocked (pytest-socket).
2. Monitor network activity while running launch, import, record payment, dashboard view and CSV export.
3. Inspect configuration for outbound endpoints.
test_cases.expected: Zero outbound connections occur across the entire workflow; every step completes with no network-dependent error; no outbound endpoint or cloud service is configured anywhere.

test_cases.title: UAT: owner verifies reinvestment free-up behavior
test_cases.steps:
1. Owner opens the reinvestment and duplicate-deduction view on a portfolio with Completed, On-going and Danger bonds.
2. Owner checks the freed principal for the Completed bond and the deduction sources.
3. Owner records pass/fail with a screenshot.
test_cases.expected: Owner confirms the Completed bond's principal is reported fully available to reinvest and that duplicate deductions are drawn only from On-going and Danger bonds.

test_cases.title: UAT: owner compares watch list against the Excel workbook
test_cases.steps:
1. Owner opens the watch list view next to the source workbook watch-list sheet.
2. Compare discount, TDS, per-month, qty TL and 12-month totals for a sample of bonds.
3. Record every mismatch.
test_cases.expected: Owner confirms computed values match the Excel watch-list outputs for every sampled bond; any mismatch is filed as a defect rather than accepted.

test_cases.title: UAT: exported CSV opens cleanly in a spreadsheet application
test_cases.steps:
1. Owner exports the dashboard dataset and the Home Plan dataset as CSV.
2. Open both files in Excel or LibreOffice.
3. Check rupee amounts and column alignment.
test_cases.expected: Both files open with no encoding errors; rupee amounts and all columns parse into the correct cells with no mojibake.

test_cases.title: UAT: dashboard refreshes on reload without open/save/restart
test_cases.steps:
1. Owner notes the current dashboard totals.
2. Owner records a payment elsewhere in the app.
3. Owner reloads the dashboard with no file open, save or server restart.
4. Owner compares figures.
test_cases.expected: The reloaded dashboard shows the updated figures, and the owner confirms no open, save or restart event was needed.

test_cases.title: UAT: launch and core features on Windows, Linux and macOS
test_cases.steps:
1. On a Windows, a Linux and a macOS desktop with only Python and a browser, run the documented launch command.
2. Exercise launch, import, record payment, dashboard view and CSV export on each OS.
3. Record results per OS.
test_cases.expected: The dashboard loads and all core features work on every OS with no build tooling and no OS-specific failure. REMOTE marker: this needs three physical/VM machines, which no local runner and no CI (none configured) can provide, so it is an owner-executed check.

test_cases.title: UAT: database file portability to a second machine
test_cases.steps:
1. Copy the app folder including the SQLite database file from machine A to machine B.
2. Open the app on machine B.
3. Search the app folder on machine A for any other persistence artifacts (second DB, cache file, external service).
test_cases.expected: Machine B shows the same bonds, payments and dashboard figures with no migration or server step; no second database, cache file or external service holds state. REMOTE marker: requires a genuine second machine, unreachable by local pytest and with no CI configured.

test_cases.title: Regression: full pytest suite rerun keeps prior green and reports L1 honestly
test_cases.steps:
1. After any code change, run the full pytest suite from the project root.
2. Verify the D5 fixture matrix, month-window boundaries, import reconciliation, CSV export and error-surfacing groups.
3. Confirm the L1 reconciliation test still reports pending_baseline.
test_cases.expected: All previously green tests remain green; the L1 reconciliation test (TC-26) is still reported as pending_baseline and is never counted as passing; any new failure blocks the change.

test_cases.title: Regression: quirk-fix sweep after refactors
test_cases.steps:
1. After any refactor, re-run the four quirk-fix verifications: visible errors, no hardcoded month windows, always-live dashboard, row-per-payment ledger.
2. Re-inspect the schema for month columns.
3. Re-render the grid at a simulated current month beyond Feb-2027.
test_cases.expected: All four quirks remain fixed: errors visible, windows dynamic, dashboard live on reload, ledger stores payments as rows with no month columns anywhere; the suite is green apart from the pending L1 baseline test.
